newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN LEAGUE MATCHES AT THE WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN LEAGUE MATCHES AT THE WEEKEND.

text.p: Italian serie A games at the weekend (league standings in parentheses, all kick-off times GMT):

Full strength Roma may cause problems for league leaders Juventus, without midfielder Antonio Conte, defender Moreno Torricelli and striker Alessandro Del Piero, all injured, and the suspended Croat striker Alen Boksic. Michele Padovano and Christian Vieri lead the Juventus attack while Argentine Abel Balbo and Francesco Totti head Roma's strike force.

Milan should be at full strength with Paolo Maldini back in defence and Croat Zvonimir Boban returning to midfield. Argentine Gabriel Batistuta and Anselmo Robbiati lead the Fiorentina attack, while Liberian George Weah and Marco Simone are the front men for Milan. Swede Stefan Schwarz of Fiorentina and Milan goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi are both suspended, with Rossi due to be replaced by Angelo Pagotto.

This looks like a play-off for second place. Parma will be without suspended Croat striker Mario Stanic but he is the only significant absentee. Argentine Hernan Crespo and Enrico Chiesa lead Parma's attack while Inter may rest players with a view to their UEFA Cup return leg game against Belgium's Anderlecht, fielding Marco Branco alongside Chilean Ivan Zamorano in attack with Nicola Berti in midfield and Alessandro Pistone in defence. In six games at the Tardini in Parma, Inter have yet to win.

Could be a good game between two in-form sides. Bologna, beaten 3-2 by Fiorentina last Sunday, field their familiar three-man attack of Carlo Nervo, Russian Igor Kolyvanov and Swede Kennet Andersson. Napoli will again be without injured Brazilian Andre Cruz, while compatriot Beto lines up in attack alongside Alfredo Aglietti.

Vicenza made a welcome return to form last week to beat Udinese 2-0 and may prove too strong for the increasingly desperate Cagliari. Both sides are missing suspended Urguyan strikers, Paolo Montero for Vicenza and Dario Silva for Cagliari.

This could be a tough test for Lazio against an Atalanta side who underlined their current form with a 4-0 drubbing of Sampdoria last Sunday. Lazio are without Australian midfielder Paul Okon as well as international strikers Giuseppe Signori and Pierluigi Casiraghi, all injured. In contrast, Atalanta field their potent trio of Domenico Morfeo, Gigi Lentini and Filippo Inzaghi, leading goalscorer on 18.

With just one point from their last four games, Sampdoria badly need to stop the rot, and second from bottom Reggiana could present the perfect opportunity. Sampdoria will be without suspended Yugoslav defender Sinisa Mihajlovic but field Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella in attack. Reggiana look to Russian striker Igor Simutenkov.
Relegation battle No. 1. German Oliver Bierhoff and Paolo Poggi to do the damage for Udinese, Croat Milan Rapajic and Marco Negri to reply for Perugia.
Relegation battle No. 2. Filippo Maniero and Nicola Zannini to do the damage for Verona, Pasquale Luiso and Gian Pietro Piovani to reply for Piacenza.
